title: The Golden Age of Groups (Factions & Breakups)
theme: The 90s were defined by groups — but keeping track of who was in what group, who went solo, and who replaced who is incredibly difficult.
narrativePurpose: Test the depth of the group member canon — lineup changes, departure histories, formation stories, and the splinter factions that defined 90s R&B.
toneProgression: Core member identification → lineup changes and departure history → pre-fame iterations and formation archaeology

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 1-9-9-1 — the year group R&B hit its first commercial peak. Boyz II Men's Cooleyhighharmony and Jodeci's Forever My Lady arrived within months of each other, establishing the vocal group as the decade's dominant format.

rounds.name: RADIO HITS
rounds.description: Core member identification. The Group Member distractor archetype is at full power here — four names on the screen, all of them were in 90s R&B groups. Only one was in THIS group.

questions.question: Destiny's Child's classic stable lineup consisted of Beyoncé Knowles, Kelly Rowland, and which third member?

metadata.fact: Michelle Williams joined Destiny's Child in 2000 alongside Farrah Franklin, filling two vacancies left by LeToya Luckett and LaTavia Roberson. After Franklin's departure five months later, the trio of Beyoncé, Kelly, and Michelle became the group's definitive and most successful lineup.
metadata.storyHook: All four choices were in Destiny's Child at some point. Only one stayed long enough to make 'Survivor.'
metadata.sourceNotes: Destiny's Child official discography. Rolling Stone retrospective. Columbia Records press archives.
metadata.hostNote: Use all four DC members as distractors — LeToya, LaTavia, Farrah, and Michelle. Maximum trap potential.

questions.question: En Vogue's original four-member lineup included Cindy Herron, Maxine Jones, and Terry Ellis alongside which fourth vocalist who later departed?

metadata.fact: Dawn Robinson was a founding member of En Vogue from their formation in Oakland in 1989 — she departed in 1997 before the recording of 'EV3,' citing creative and personal conflicts. Her departure changed the group's dynamic permanently.
metadata.storyHook: The four-part harmony that launched a thousand imitators. Then one of the four left, and nothing sounded quite the same.
metadata.sourceNotes: En Vogue official biography. EastWest Records press archives. Billboard chart documentation.

questions.question: SWV — the trio behind 'Right Here (Human Nature Remix)' — consisted of Coko and Lelee alongside which third member?

metadata.fact: SWV — Sisters With Voices — consisted of Coko (Cheryl Gamble), Lelee (Leanne Lyons), and Taj (Tamara Johnson). Taj was the group's most reserved presence publicly but contributed significantly to their vocal arrangements.
metadata.storyHook: Coko had the voice. Lelee had the presence. Taj held it all together.
metadata.sourceNotes: SWV official biography. RCA Records press materials. AllMusic artist documentation.
metadata.hostNote: T-Boz and Chilli are TLC — maximum distractor potential across girl groups.

sources.title: Who Is In SWV? – Bravo TV

questions.question: Bell Biv DeVoe was formed from New Edition by Ricky Bell and Michael Bivins alongside which third member?

metadata.fact: Bell Biv DeVoe took their name from the first letters of Ricky Bell, Michael Bivins, and Ronnie DeVoe's surnames — the three New Edition members who weren't pursuing solo careers. Bobby Brown, Ralph Tresvant, and Johnny Gill all went solo, leaving the trio to reinvent themselves under the New Jack Swing sound.
metadata.storyHook: Six members of New Edition. Three went solo. Three stuck together and named themselves after their last names. Only one answer here was actually in Bell Biv DeVoe.
metadata.sourceNotes: Bell Biv DeVoe official biography. MCA Records press archives. VH1 Behind the Music documentation.
metadata.hostNote: All four choices are actual New Edition members — peak distractor archetype.

questions.question: Xscape — the Atlanta quartet behind 'Just Kickin' It' — featured founding member LaTocha Scott alongside which sibling who also sang in the group?

metadata.fact: Xscape's four members included two pairs — LaTocha Scott and her sister Tamika Scott, alongside Tameka 'Tiny' Cottle and Kandi Burruss. LaTocha was the group's lead vocalist; Tamika, her younger sister, sang harmonies and occasionally stepped into lead roles.
metadata.storyHook: All four choices are connected to Xscape. Only one is specifically LaTocha Scott's sister.
metadata.sourceNotes: Xscape official biography. So So Def Records press archives. Billboard chart documentation.
metadata.hostNote: All four choices are real Xscape members or closely associated — strongest distractor trap in Round 1.

sources.title: XSCAPE Member LaTocha Scott Reconciles With Sister Tamika – BET

questions.question: Which Destiny's Child member — who appeared in the 'Say My Name' music video — departed the group after just five months in 2000?

metadata.fact: Farrah Franklin joined Destiny's Child in February 2000 as one of two replacements for LeToya Luckett and LaTavia Roberson — she appeared in the 'Say My Name' video but missed promotional appearances citing illness, and was dismissed by August 2000, leaving the classic trio intact.
metadata.storyHook: She filmed the video. She missed the tour. Five months in Destiny's Child was all she got.
metadata.sourceNotes: Columbia Records press documentation. Destiny's Child official history. Billboard reporting on 2000 lineup change.

questions.question: LSG's 'L' — Gerald Levert — is the son of which legendary O'Jays lead vocalist?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 1 OF 3 — GERALD LEVERT'S FATHER'S NAME

metadata.fact: Eddie Levert is the lead vocalist of The O'Jays and the father of Gerald Levert — making the Leverts one of R&B's most accomplished family dynasties. Gerald's participation in LSG with Keith Sweat and Johnny Gill placed him at the center of 90s New Jack Swing's supergroup era.
metadata.storyHook: His father sang 'For the Love of Money.' He sang 'My Body.' The Levert name was everywhere in R&B.
metadata.sourceNotes: O'Jays official biography. Gerald Levert biographical records. Philadelphia International Records documentation.

rounds.name: DEEP CUTS
rounds.description: Lineup changes, departure dates, album titles from incomplete lineups, and the supergroups nobody asked for but everyone loved.

questions.question: En Vogue's 1997 album — recorded as a trio after Dawn Robinson's departure — was titled what?

metadata.fact: EV3 — shorthand for En Vogue Three — was released on EastWest Records in 1997 and debuted at #7 on the Billboard 200. Despite the personnel change, the album went platinum on the strength of 'Don't Let Go (Love)' and demonstrated the group's commercial resilience without Robinson.
metadata.storyHook: They named the album after how many of them were left. That is a level of brutal honesty that most groups don't attempt.
metadata.sourceNotes: EV3 liner notes (EastWest, 1997). Billboard chart archives. Discogs release page.

questions.question: The LSG supergroup's debut 1997 lead single — which became a staple on late-night R&B radio — was titled what?

metadata.fact: 'My Body' was LSG's debut lead single from their 1997 self-titled album — it spent seven weeks at #1 on the Billboard R&B chart and peaked at #4 on the Hot 100, establishing the supergroup as a genuine commercial force rather than a novelty.
metadata.storyHook: Three solo careers, one song, one chart-topper. The supergroup formula worked exactly as advertised.
metadata.sourceNotes: Billboard Hot 100 and R&B chart archives. LSG official discography. EastWest Records press materials.

questions.question: Which Boyz II Men member — the group's distinctive bass vocalist who sang 'Thank You' — departed in 2003 after being diagnosed with multiple sclerosis?

metadata.fact: Michael McCary — known for his remarkable bass range that anchored Boyz II Men's four-part harmony — left the group in 2003 after his multiple sclerosis diagnosis made touring and performing increasingly difficult. His departure reduced the group to the trio that continues performing today.
metadata.storyHook: The lowest voice in the room. The one that made the harmony complete. Gone in 2003, and the sound changed forever.
metadata.sourceNotes: Boyz II Men official statements on McCary's departure. Billboard reporting (2003). Michael McCary biographical records.
metadata.hostNote: All four choices are the actual Boyz II Men members — maximum distractor potential.

questions.question: Xscape's Tameka 'Tiny' Cottle — whose voice was among the most distinctive in 90s R&B — went on to marry which Atlanta rapper?

metadata.fact: Tameka 'Tiny' Cottle married Clifford 'T.I.' Harris in 2010 — their relationship was documented on the VH1 reality series 'T.I. & Tiny: The Family Hustle,' keeping Tiny in the public eye long after Xscape's initial commercial run ended.
metadata.storyHook: She sang soprano with Xscape. She became half of Atlanta's most televised couple. The voice never changed.
metadata.sourceNotes: T.I. & Tiny: The Family Hustle official documentation. VH1 press materials. Atlanta Journal-Constitution reporting.

questions.question: SWV's lead vocalist — who performed under the stage name 'Coko' — has what birth name?

metadata.fact: Coko's birth name is Cheryl Gamble — she adopted the stage name from a childhood nickname. Her gospel-trained soprano voice was the distinguishing instrument of SWV's sound, setting her apart from the era's more polished, production-driven vocalists.
metadata.storyHook: All four choices are real Cheryls in R&B. Only one of them was Coko.
metadata.sourceNotes: SWV official biography. RCA Records press materials. Coko solo career documentation.
metadata.hostNote: The all-Cheryl distractor set is intentional — maximum confusion for anyone who knows their 90s R&B Cheryls.

questions.question: Dru Hill — the Baltimore quartet known for 'In My Bed' and 'How Deep Is Your Love' — took their group name from which Baltimore landmark?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 2 OF 3 — THE BALTIMORE LANDMARK BEHIND DRU HILL

metadata.fact: Dru Hill took their name from Druid Hill — the Baltimore neighborhood and park — as a nod to their city of origin. The park is home to the Maryland Zoo and is one of the oldest landscaped public parks in the United States.
metadata.storyHook: They shortened it by two letters and made it a group name. The park didn't mind.
metadata.sourceNotes: Dru Hill official biography. Island Records press materials. Baltimore City geographic records.

reserve.question: The supergroup LSG took its name from the initials of its three members — Gerald Levert, Johnny Gill, and which third artist?

metadata.fact: LSG stood for Levert, Sweat, Gill — Gerald Levert, Keith Sweat, and Johnny Gill. The three veteran R&B artists combined their surnames to form the name of their 1997 supergroup collaboration, which produced the hit 'My Body.'
metadata.storyHook: Three surnames. One acronym. LSG made it obvious who was in the room — if you knew your R&B.

rounds.name: HIDDEN GEMS
rounds.description: Pre-fame group names, formation archaeology, and the managers and fathers who shaped everything from the outside.

questions.question: Before Destiny's Child existed, a young Beyoncé Knowles performed in a youth group that competed on Star Search in 1993. What was that group called?

metadata.fact: Girl's Tyme — which included a young Beyoncé Knowles, Kelly Rowland, and LeToya Luckett — competed on Star Search in 1993 and lost to a rock band called Skeleton Crew. The loss was devastating to the group and its young members, but it became the primary motivation for Mathew Knowles to revamp the lineup and redirect the group — a reorganization that eventually produced Destiny's Child.
metadata.storyHook: They lost to a rock band called Skeleton Crew. Then they regrouped. Then they became the biggest girl group of the decade. Beyoncé even quoted the loss in 'Flawless.' The defeat earned its own monument.
metadata.sourceNotes: Star Search broadcast archives (1993). Destiny's Child official biography. Beyoncé 'Flawless' sample documentation. Mathew Knowles management records.

questions.question: Destiny's Child's manager — who also negotiated the group's high-profile lineup changes and is Beyoncé's father — was named what?

metadata.fact: Mathew Knowles managed Destiny's Child from their Girl's Tyme days through their commercial peak — he oversaw the 2000 lineup change that dismissed LeToya Luckett and LaTavia Roberson, a decision that generated considerable controversy and litigation but ultimately preserved the group's commercial trajectory.
metadata.storyHook: He managed the group, negotiated the departures, and happened to be the lead singer's father. The conflict of interest was the point.
metadata.sourceNotes: Mathew Knowles management records. Rolling Stone reporting on 2000 Destiny's Child lineup change. Columbia Records documentation.

questions.question: Jodeci's K-Ci and JoJo Hailey — who later formed their own duo — are brothers originally from which small North Carolina city?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — THE NORTH CAROLINA CITY K-CI AND JOJO CALLED HOME

metadata.fact: Cedric 'K-Ci' Hailey and Joel 'JoJo' Hailey were born and raised in Monroe, North Carolina — a small city southeast of Charlotte — before relocating and eventually forming Jodeci with the DeGrate brothers. Their gospel upbringing in Monroe's church community formed the vocal foundation they brought to both Jodeci and their duo career.
metadata.storyHook: Monroe, North Carolina produced two of the greatest voices of the 90s R&B era. The city is still waiting for its credit.
metadata.sourceNotes: K-Ci & JoJo biographical records. Jodeci formation documentation. Monroe NC city records.

reserve.question: K-Ci & JoJo's debut album — which contained their chart-topping ballad 'All My Life' — was titled what?

metadata.fact: Love Always was released on MCA Records in June 1997 as K-Ci & JoJo's debut duo album. 'All My Life' was the album's third single, released in early 1998 — it topped the Billboard Hot 100 for three weeks and became the defining record of their career.
metadata.sourceNotes: Love Always liner notes (MCA Records, 1997). Billboard Hot 100 chart archives. MCA Records release documentation.

reserve.question: Dru Hill's Sisqo — who later had a massive solo hit with 'Thong Song' — has what birth name?

metadata.fact: Sisqo's legal birth name is Mark Althavan Andrews — he adopted the stage name Sisqo from a childhood nickname. His 2000 solo smash 'Thong Song' reached #3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and became one of the defining pop-R&B crossover moments of the era.
metadata.sourceNotes: Sisqo biographical records. Dru Hill official biography. Island/Def Soul Records press materials.
